topic: Introduction to Holomorphic Dynamics: Iterated Complex Functions

outline.topic: Introduction to Holomorphic Dynamics: Iterated Complex Functions

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Complex Plane
sections.content: Briefly define complex numbers z = x + iy and the concept of a holomorphic function f(z) as a mapping that preserves angles (conformal). Visualize the complex plane as a canvas for transformation.
sections.example: Visualizing f(z) = z² as an 'expansion and rotation' map on the complex plane grid.

sections.title: The Concept of Iteration
sections.content: Introduce the idea of functional iteration: f^n(z) = f(f(...f(z)...)). Explain that we are looking for the 'long-term behavior' of a point as it is repeatedly plugged back into the function.
sections.example: An ant walking on a surface where each step is governed by the same rule f(z); we want to see if the ant escapes to infinity or gets trapped in a cycle.

sections.title: Defining the Fatou and Julia Sets
sections.content: Distinguish between stability and chaos. The Fatou set consists of points where nearby orbits behave similarly (stable). The Julia set is the 'boundary of chaos' where small differences in initial position lead to wildly different outcomes (sensitive dependence).
sections.example: Using a color-coded 'Attractor Map' where stable regions are smooth colors and the Julia set appears as a complex, jagged, fractal boundary.

sections.title: Core Example: The Quadratic Map f(z) = z² + c
sections.content: Examine the simplest non-linear iteration. Explain how varying the constant 'c' completely changes the geometry of the Julia set, demonstrating how a simple equation creates infinite complexity.
sections.example: An animation showing the 'Mandelbrot set' as a map: as the parameter 'c' moves, the Julia set transitions from a simple circle to a 'Dragon' or 'Dendrite' shape.

sections.title: Conclusion and Real-world Intuition
sections.content: Summarize how iteration reveals order within chaos. Connect this to physical systems like fluid turbulence or biological growth patterns.
sections.example: A 'Feedback Loop' diagram showing how digital image compression algorithms utilize similar recursive fractal geometry principles.
